title: Arkham nine-character ward stress (extended run)
intent: Same large-cast stress as arkham_multi_character_stress but with a longer beat budget so staff (Arkham, Karlsson, Cash) and patients cycle more often under perimeter-alarm uncertainty; useful for evidence on authoritative assertion patterns.
opening_description: Late evening stretches toward night on Arkham's secure clinical wing: fluorescent hum, locked doors, disinfectant and old stone. Staff and high-profile patients have been held in a prolonged corridor cluster after a partial lockdown drill—radios still trade conflicting fragments about a fence line and who might have been near it. Overtime orderlies swap in; fatigue and boredom sharpen some inmates while others go brittle. Dr. Arkham and Dr. Karlsson keep trying to impose a single narrative; Cash keeps a hand near his belt; Selina, Ivy, Harley, Magpie, Nocturna, and Jane Doe remain under escort or observation with uneven privileges and old grudges. Nobody has been shown full incident video; rumors have had time to fork.
trigger_text: A PA line cuts in mid-sentence—static, then silence. Cash snaps, 'Nobody moves until we know if that was a test or a breach.' Ivy murmurs something only Selina is close enough to catch. Harley grins like she heard anyway. Arkham raises his voice just enough to cut through the whispers: 'We need one clear chain of fact, not nine competing stories. Who was where when the alarm tripped—and I want it coherent enough to survive a chart note.' Karlsson's eyes flick toward the patients, measuring who is already fraying.

seed_issue.description: Conflicting partial information about a perimeter or lockdown event; staff must assert control while patients test boundaries; extended time in corridor increases pressure for definitive statements.
